prerequisites: Students must know and handle with ease the principles of mass conservation, Newton's 2nd Law and Thermodynamics 1st Law and be familiar with the properties and behavior of fluids. The subjects in the degree where these essential prior requirements are taught are Physics, Fluid Mechanics and Thermodynamics.
To enroll in this subject, it is necessary to pass or be enrolled in all subjects from courses prior to the course in which this subject is located.

learning_outcomes.text: Understand the basic aspects of fluid machinery
Acquire skills on the process of sizing pumping installations and fluid machinery

assessment_rules: For continuous assessment in the first opportunity, attendance at evaluable tests is mandatory, and a minimum of 40% is required in each test to pass the subject. If the sum of qualifications exceeds 5.0 but the minimum for each test is not reached, the grade recorded will be 4.5. For the second opportunity in continuous assessment, students can retake tests with a weight greater than 20% that were not passed (those with a score below 50%), while grades for passed tests are maintained; a minimum of 40% is still required in each retaken test. For global assessment in both opportunities, students must pass a single global evaluation exam covering 100% of the grade. Unethical behavior (copying, plagiarism, unauthorized electronic devices, etc.) will result in a global grade of 0.0 for the academic year.
